instructions.content: OCR first, extraction second: PyMuPDF does not handle all PDFs equally, so switch to Mathpix for high-precision needs or pre-inspect output before running AI extraction.
Prompts determine quality: ALWAYS review the raw LLM output before saving, because ambiguous headers or merged cells can silently corrupt values.
Batch is not atomic: ALWAYS check the per-file success log, because failed files are listed at the end and may need re-running individually.
Install dependencies on first run as described in the setup reference.
Configure environment variables (EXTRACTOR_API_KEY, EXTRACTOR_BASE_URL, EXTRACTOR_MODEL, and optionally MATHPIX_APP_ID and MATHPIX_APP_KEY) before running.
Use a preset template (enzyme, experiment or review) with ./scripts/extractor.py <pdf> --template <name> -o <file>.
For needs the presets do not cover, pass a custom prompt with -p.
Use --format csv to write CSV output.
Use --ocr mathpix for high-precision extraction.
Use ./scripts/batch_extract.py <input-folder> <output-folder> --template <name> --format <fmt> to process a folder of PDFs.
Use --print to show extracted results in the terminal for inspection.
NEVER skip validating extracted output before saving to a database: print the results and spot-check at least 3 rows against the source PDF.
NEVER pass a scanned image-only PDF to PyMuPDF without warning the user; check that the extracted text length is reasonable and switch to --ocr mathpix if it is empty or very short.
NEVER use a custom prompt that omits output format instructions, such as the table columns and delimiter.
NEVER treat batch output as complete without reviewing the failed-files list; re-run failed files individually with --print.
NEVER store EXTRACTOR_API_KEY in plain text in a script or committed file; ALWAYS use environment variables or a dotenv file excluded from version control.
NEVER assume Mathpix is available; ALWAYS confirm both MATHPIX_APP_ID and MATHPIX_APP_KEY are set before using it, and optionally fall back to PyMuPDF.
Do not use this skill when the paper is already in a machine-readable format (XML, JSON, HTML); parse it directly.
Do not use this skill for abstracts, titles, real-time citation counts or DOI resolution; use semantic-scholar-search.
Do not rely on results from low-resolution scanned PDFs with no embedded text when Mathpix is unavailable; they will be unreliable.
